attribution.note: Marcus's own closing sentence in his own post. It is not a quote of anyone else.

semantics.note: Two parts. 'Lead is slipping' is a firm present-tense observation. 'It looks their financing is, too' is hedged as an appearance, and the drafter keeps that hedge with 'appears'.

contract.note: Reading 'lead' as share of usage or enterprise share is an ordinary, fair reading, and the contract judges the two parts separately. The financing part is hedged by 'it looks', so it cannot be firmly upheld. The evidence on it also points both ways.

evidence.note: Menlo Ventures, Dec 2025: OpenAI's enterprise API share fell to 27%, behind Anthropic. This is an independent measurement within the period.
Similarweb via Tom's Guide, Jan 2026: ChatGPT's share of chatbot traffic fell from about 86% to about 65% as Gemini rose.
WSJ report via Fortune: Nvidia's $100B plan had stalled. This is a sign of financing trouble before the post.
In the same article, Huang said Nvidia would still make a 'huge' investment in the current round. Financing was not drying up.
Reuters, Jan 27: SoftBank was in talks to invest up to $30B more, as part of a round of up to $100B.

reviews.rationale: The 'lead slipping' part holds: OpenAI lost enterprise API share (e1) and chatbot traffic share (e2) in the period. The financing part is hedged ('it looks'), and the evidence is split. Nvidia's plan stalled (e3), but Nvidia still promised a huge investment (e4) and SoftBank was in talks to add $30B (e5). So the financing part is not upheld.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Will be skittish' is an unqualified forecast about how other investors would behave. The Nvidia premise is stated as fact, and the SoftBank premise is only a possibility. It is better classed as a forecast than as a causal claim, and no deadline was stated.

contract.note: The contract sets a window to 2026-04-30 and a causal axis that the speaker did not supply. It has no early-resolution rule. 'Skittish' has no measure: the primary round could contradict it while the secondary market could support it.

evidence.note: Feb 27, 2026: a $110B round, with Nvidia and SoftBank at $30B each and Amazon as a large new investor at $50B.
Mar 31 update: the round closed at $122B, including $3B from new individual investors.
There was weak secondary-market demand in March, but the article attributes it to valuation and to money moving to Anthropic, not to Nvidia or SoftBank.
This is evidence of the premise only: Nvidia's $100B plan stalled. It is not evidence of the outcome.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no stated deadline, and the contract has no early-resolution rule, so it cannot be scored yet. The evidence leans against it: the round closed at $122B with Nvidia and SoftBank investing and new backers joining (e1, e2). Secondary-market weakness (e3) is not tied to the cause he named.
